records.title: Altitude decompression sickness: 100 years of research, current prevention and treatment
records.locator: Final paragraph on author chamber ultrasound analysis
records.note: Author cites own chamber ultrasound analysis in 123 people at 2.5–12 km. No reports of clinical endpoints, exposure-level linkage or outcome window are given for this sample. General historical totals and risk estimates elsewhere in the text are context.

records.title: Possibility of the development of decompression sickness during testing of G suits
records.locator: Author abstract, results and decompression conditions
records.note: Twenty-nine tests with DCS among 1,179 and 26 affected people among 193 describe the same chamber series. The abstract does not assign groups or document clinical criteria, timing, repeat participant identities or fixed follow-up.

observations.note: Twenty-nine tests with DCS. Each denominator unit is a test, and multiple tests per person are possible. Related experimental series cannot be ruled out.
observations.outcome_window: During the tests. Postexposure follow-up and ascertainment criteria not stated.

observations.note: Twenty-six affected people in the same series. This person margin overlaps the 29 tests with DCS. Retain the source's printed 13.4% and exact reported counts without substitution.
observations.outcome_window: During the tests. Postexposure follow-up and ascertainment criteria not stated.

records.title: Instructive story of one high-altitude flight: decompression sickness in an aircraft crew and its consequences
records.note: Publisher-supplied DOI. Crossref returned 404 for this identifier. The public abstract names one pilot with severe altitude DCS after Su-24M cabin depressurization. A separate journal version describes the same event. The abstract does not specify exact flight duration, aircraft or cabin altitude, other clinical cases or the crew at risk.

observations.locator: Author abstract and same-case Academy abstract, both pp. 50–54
observations.note: The abstract explicitly describes one severe pilot case. The scope of the title refers to the crew, but the abstract gives no crew count or additional adjudicated cases. The Academy abstract is a second report of this case.
observations.outcome_window: Exact onset, clinical assessment and follow-up times unavailable in the public abstract.

records.title: Early Human Pathophysiological Responses to Exertional Hypobaric Decompression Stress
records.note: Phase 1 follow-up publication of the 15-person repeated dispatcher chamber trial. It corroborates the three existing DCS cases at 29 and 37 min on ascent 1 and 60 min on ascent 2, and reports the number of participants with heavy persistent VGE across the sequence.

observations.note: Person-level author characterization. No grade-specific count or additional clinical DCS events are inferred. Some participants stopped early.
observations.outcome_window: During the same-day paired chamber sequence, especially on the first ascent.

records.locator: Results and Discussion, text immediately after Figure 1
records.note: Existing v1.22 source. Three participants had musculoskeletal DCS symptoms without a detected bubble signal at reported pressures of 225, 245 and 256 mmHg. This subgroup sits within the same study as the 42 affected participants.
